mainTopic: Whose תחום does an animal or a jointly owned item follow on יום טוב, and does בְּרֵירָה (retroactive designation) apply?
overview: Our משנה says an animal is 'like the feet of its owner' on יום טוב, even if he handed it to his son or a shepherd. The גמרא reconciles this with רבי דוסא, who says it follows the shepherd. רבי דוסא means a town with one shepherd, and the משנה means a town with two shepherds. That same split explains how רבי יוחנן can rule like רבי דוסא and still follow a סתם משנה. A ברייתא then teaches that a robe borrowed by two partners may only go where both of them may walk. Next, רב and שמואל argue about a barrel and an animal bought in partnership, which turns on בְּרֵירָה: whether a later division counts as if each share was designated from the start. רב's distinction for the animal is challenged, and he stays silent. The גמרא then reports רבי הושעיא and רבי יוחנן on בְּרֵירָה and reverses their views (אפוך) because of a משנה about a corpse in a house. Finally, it tests whether רבי יוחנן accepts בְּרֵירָה at least in rabbinic laws, using איו's ברייתא about עירוב. That challenge continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Our משנה seems to go against רבי דוסא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proposes that our משנה, which says an animal given to a shepherd stays 'like the feet of the owner,' disagrees with a ברייתא of רבי דוסא, who says it becomes 'like the feet of the shepherd.'
steps.simpleTranslation: [Shall we say our משנה] is not like רבי דוסא? For a ברייתא teaches: רבי דוסא says (and some say אבא שאול says): If someone buys an animal from his friend before יום טוב, even if the seller only handed it over on יום טוב, it is like the feet of the buyer. And if someone hands his animal to a shepherd, even if he only handed it over on יום טוב, it is like the feet of the shepherd.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its suggestion that our משנה conflicts with רבי דוסא. It quotes the ברייתא that shows his opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On יום טוב, an object or animal may only travel as far as the person it 'belongs to' for this purpose may walk. Our משנה says an animal given to a shepherd still follows the owner. רבי דוסא says it follows the shepherd, even though the handover happened only on יום טוב itself. So the two sources seem to give opposite rulings for the same case.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Like the feet of': the item may only go where that person may walk on יום טוב.
The buyer.
The shepherd.
He handed it over.
'And some say': an alternate attribution of the same teaching.

steps.confusionAlert: This amud begins in the middle of a sentence. The words just before it ('לימא מתניתין', 'shall we say our משנה') are what turn 'דלא כרבי דוסא' into a question the גמרא is testing. It is not a final ruling.

phrases.english: is not in accordance with Rabbi Dosa,
phrases.notes: Continues the earlier 'Shall we say our משנה...'

phrases.english: as it is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Dosa says,
and some say: Abba Shaul says,

phrases.aramaic: הַלּוֹקֵחַ בְּהֵמָה מֵחֲבֵרוֹ מֵעֶרֶב יוֹם טוֹב,
phrases.english: one who buys an animal from his friend on the eve of the Festival,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא מְסָרָהּ לוֹ אֶלָּא בְּיוֹם טוֹב —
phrases.english: even though he only handed it to him on the Festival,
it is like the feet of the buyer.
And one who hands an animal to a shepherd,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁלֹּא מְסָרָהּ לוֹ אֶלָּא בְּיוֹם טוֹב —
phrases.english: even though he only handed it to him on the Festival,
it is like the feet of the shepherd.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּלָא כְּרַבִּי דּוֹסָא, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the proposal on the previous amud that the משנה is not like רבי דוסא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that an animal handed to a shepherd stays 'כרגלי הבעלים'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי דוסא explicitly rules that an animal handed to a shepherd, even on יום טוב, follows the shepherd. That is the opposite of the משנה.

steps.title: One shepherd versus two shepherds
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה can match רבי דוסא. רבי דוסא speaks of a town with one shepherd, and the משנה speaks of a town with two shepherds.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say [the משנה follows] רבי דוסא, and there is no difficulty. Here [the ברייתא] is about one shepherd. There [the משנה] is about two shepherds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא removes the conflict. It shows that each source is talking about a different situation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With only one shepherd in town, the owner knows from before יום טוב exactly who will get the animal. So the animal's boundary is tied to that shepherd from the start. With two shepherds, it is not yet decided who will take the animal, so it stays tied to the owner.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You can even say': the next source can still fit the opinion that seemed to be contradicted.
'And it is not difficult': there is no real contradiction.
'Here... there': each source is assigned to a different case.
One shepherd.

phrases.english: You can even say it follows Rabbi Dosa,
and it is not difficult:
here, with one shepherd,
there, with two shepherds.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי דּוֹסָא, וְלָא קַשְׁיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases (אוקימתא): each source refers to a different situation.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and רבי דוסא rule differently on the very same case.
steps.terutzMaskana: No dispute exists. One shepherd means the animal follows the shepherd. Two shepherds means it follows the owner.

steps.title: The משנה's wording supports the two-shepherd reading
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says 'to his son or to the shepherd.' That wording shows the owner had not decided in advance who would receive the animal, which fits the case of two shepherds.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording is also precise, since it teaches: 'to his son or to the shepherd.' Learn from it [that this is correct].
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support for its answer from the exact words of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'his son or the shepherd' suggests that the recipient was undecided when יום טוב began. That is exactly the situation with two shepherds. So the משנה's own language supports the split made in step 2.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is also precise': the wording itself supports this reading.
'Since it teaches.'
'Learn from it': the point is proven.

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה and רבי דוסא do not argue. In a one-shepherd town, the animal follows the shepherd. In a town with two shepherds (where the recipient is undecided), it follows the owner.

phrases.english: It is also precise,
as it teaches: 'to his son or to the shepherd,'
phrases.notes: The 'or' implies the recipient was not decided in advance.

phrases.english: Learn from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: דַּיְקָא נָמֵי דְּקָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer given in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that the משנה refers to a case with two shepherds.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן rules like Rabbi Dosa
steps.stepSummary: רבה בר בר חנה reports in the name of רבי יוחנן that the הלכה follows רבי דוסא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה בר בר חנה said in the name of רבי יוחנן: The הלכה is like רבי דוסא.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement is brought: a ruling that the הלכה follows רבי דוסא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets the practical law: an animal handed to a shepherd follows the shepherd's boundary. The next step will question whether this fits with another rule of רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law.
An אמורא who transmits teachings of רבי יוחנן.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: Rabba bar bar Chana said that Rabbi Yochanan said:
The halakha is like Rabbi Dosa.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from showing that the sources agree to deciding the practical הלכה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The הלכה follows רבי דוסא: an animal handed to a shepherd is like the feet of the shepherd.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן seems to contradict himself
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן also holds that the הלכה follows a סתם משנה, and our unattributed משנה says animals are 'like the feet of the owner.' So how can he rule like רבי דוסא?
steps.simpleTranslation: Did רבי יוחנן really say this? But רבי יוחנן said: The הלכה follows an unattributed משנה. And we learned: 'Animals and vessels are like the feet of the owners'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's ruling by pointing to another rule of his own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's general rule is that an unattributed משנה is the הלכה. Our משנה is unattributed, and it says the animal follows the owner. That seems to contradict his ruling like רבי דוסא, who says it follows the shepherd.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And did he really say?': introduces a challenge.
'But didn't he say?'
An unattributed משנה, taught with no named author.
The owners.

phrases.english: And did Rabbi Yochanan say this?
But didn't Rabbi Yochanan say:
The halakha follows an unattributed mishna,
and we learned: 'Animals and vessels'
'are like the feet of the owners'!

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הָכִי? וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that the הלכה follows רבי דוסא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His own rule that the הלכה follows a סתם משנה would require following our משנה ('כרגלי הבעלים'), which seems to oppose רבי דוסא.

steps.title: The one-shepherd versus two-shepherd split solves this too
steps.stepSummary: Since the משנה (two shepherds) and רבי דוסא (one shepherd) discuss different cases, רבי יוחנן can follow both.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't we already establish: here it is about one shepherd, there it is about two shepherds!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by reminding us of the distinction it already made in step 2.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Because the two sources do not argue, ruling like רבי דוסא does not reject the סתם משנה. רבי יוחנן's two statements fit together.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Didn't we establish?': the גמרא points back to an earlier reading of the sources.

steps.whatToRemember: The final הלכה: in a town with one shepherd, the animal follows the shepherd (רבי דוסא). In a town with two shepherds, it follows the owner (the משנה). Both are accepted together.

phrases.english: But didn't we establish:
here, with one shepherd,
there, with two shepherds!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלָאו אוֹקֵימְנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 5 by reusing the answer from step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reapplies the earlier split of cases.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Ruling like רבי דוסא contradicts the סתם משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: No contradiction exists. Each source governs its own case, so רבי יוחנן's two rules fit together.

steps.title: Two people borrow one robe and each goes a different direction
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a robe borrowed by two partners may only be carried as far as both of them are allowed to walk.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: Two people borrowed one robe together. One wanted to wear it in the morning to the בית המדרש, and the other wanted to wear it in the evening to a wedding feast. One made an עירוב תחומין to the north, and the other made one to the south. The one whose עירוב is to the north may walk north with the robe only as far as the one whose עירוב is to the south may walk. The one whose עירוב is to the south may walk south with it only as far as the one whose עירוב is to the north may walk.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא showing that an object shared by two people can only go where both of them are allowed to go.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each borrower has a share in the robe, so the robe is bound by both of their limits at once. The northern borrower can carry it north only up to the point where the southern borrower's northern limit ends, and the same is true in the other direction. This is the same idea as 'like the feet of the owner,' applied to two owners at once.

keyTerms.meaning: They borrowed
A robe or cloak
In partnership, held jointly
Made an עירוב תחומין, setting his base for walking on שבת or יום טוב
Like the feet of, meaning limited to where that person may walk

steps.confusionAlert: Each person may walk freely within his OWN limit without the robe. The restriction applies only to carrying the shared robe, which is held to the overlap of both people's limits.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
Two people who borrowed one robe in partnership,

phrases.aramaic: זֶה לֵילֵךְ בּוֹ שַׁחֲרִית לְבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ,
phrases.english: this one to go in it in the morning to the study hall,

phrases.aramaic: וְזֶה לִיכָּנֵס בּוֹ עַרְבִית לְבֵית הַמִּשְׁתֶּה.
phrases.english: and that one to enter in it in the evening to the wedding feast.
This one made an eiruv for himself to the north,
and that one made an eiruv for himself to the south.
The one who made an eiruv for himself to the north
may walk to the north
only as far as the feet of the one who made an eiruv to the south may go.
phrases.notes: The robe is limited by the other partner's northern limit.

phrases.english: And the one who made an eiruv for himself to the south
may walk to the south
only as far as the feet of the one who made an eiruv to the north may go.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שְׁנַיִם שֶׁשָּׁאֲלוּ חָלוּק אֶחָד בְּשׁוּתָּפוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After settling how רבי יוחנן can follow both רבי דוסא and the סתם משנה, the גמרא moves to a new ברייתא about an object shared by two partners.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A jointly borrowed object may be carried only within the overlap of both partners' תחומין.

steps.title: When the two limits meet in the middle, the robe cannot move
steps.stepSummary: If each partner's limit ends exactly at the shared spot, the robe may not be moved at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if their limits meet in the middle, then neither of them may move the robe from its place.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues with an extreme case: the two partners' limits overlap only at a single point, so the robe is completely stuck.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Suppose one placed his עירוב 2,000 אמות south of the house and the other 2,000 אמות north of it. The house is then the farthest edge for each of them. Since the robe may only go where both may go, and the only shared place is the house itself, it cannot be moved anywhere.

keyTerms.meaning: They made it meet in the middle
The שבת and יום טוב walking boundary, 2,000 אמות
He may not move it

steps.whatToRemember: A shared object follows ALL of its owners. Its permitted area is only the overlap of their limits. If the overlap is just one point, the object cannot move.

phrases.english: And if they made the boundary meet in the middle,
then neither may move it from its place.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִם מִצְּעוּ אֶת הַתְּחוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same overlap rule to the most extreme case, where the overlap shrinks to zero.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the partners' limits touch only at the object's location, the object may not be moved at all.

steps.title: רב: a shared barrel is permitted, but a shared animal is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces a case of a barrel and an animal bought in partnership, and רב rules that the barrel is permitted while the animal is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: Two people bought a barrel of wine and an animal in partnership. רב said: The barrel is permitted, but the animal is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new מחלוקת between אמוראים about partners who bought a barrel and an animal together and divide them on יום טוב when they have different limits. This step gives רב's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב says each partner may take his share of the wine and carry it anywhere within his own תחום, as if that share had always been his. The animal is different, and its meat stays limited to the overlap of both partners' limits. The גמרא explains the reason for this difference in Step 12.

keyTerms.meaning: It was stated; introduces a dispute between אמוראים
They bought
A barrel of wine
An animal, here its meat after slaughter

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not whether they may divide the wine or meat on יום טוב. It is how far each partner may carry his portion afterward: within his own limit, or only within the shared overlap.

phrases.english: It was stated:
Two people who bought a barrel and an animal in partnership,
Rav said:
The barrel is permitted, but the animal is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִתְּמַר: שְׁנַיִם שֶׁלָּקְחוּ חָבִית וּבְהֵמָה בְּשׁוּתָּפוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from a borrowed robe to items that are actually owned together and divided on יום טוב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב: a jointly owned barrel may be carried by each partner within his own limit, but the animal's meat is restricted.

steps.title: שמואל: the barrel is forbidden too
steps.stepSummary: שמואל disagrees with רב and says the barrel is also limited, just like the animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: And שמואל said: The barrel is also forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל gives the other side of the מחלוקת: he treats the barrel exactly like the animal. This sets up the גמרא's coming discussion of each opinion's reasoning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to שמואל, dividing the barrel on יום טוב does not make each share count as having belonged to one partner from the start. So every portion of wine stays bound by both partners' limits, just like the robe in the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: Also, too
Forbidden, here meaning restricted to the shared limit

steps.whyThisMatters: This מחלוקת raises the question of whether a later division can define who owned which part from the beginning. The coming גמרא will analyze that idea.

phrases.english: And Shmuel said:
The barrel is also forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּשְׁמוּאֵל אָמַר: חָבִית נָמֵי אֲסוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposing view in the same מחלוקת. It agrees about the animal but disagrees about the barrel.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמואל: both the barrel and the animal stay restricted to the overlap of the partners' limits.

steps.title: רב's split ruling does not seem to fit either view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רב's position on בְּרֵירָה is. Either way, the barrel and the animal should get the same ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does רב hold? If he holds there is retroactive designation, even the animal should be permitted! And if he holds there is no retroactive designation, even the barrel should be forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב's ruling from Step 9, which permitted the barrel but forbade the animal. It argues that one consistent principle cannot produce two different results.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If יש ברירה, then after the split each partner's share is treated as having been his all along, so the shared limit should not apply to anything. If אין ברירה, both items were jointly owned when יום טוב began, so both should be limited. Permitting one and forbidding the other looks inconsistent.

keyTerms.meaning: There is retroactive designation. A later choice reveals what was true from the start.
There is no retroactive designation. A later choice does not reach back in time.
Barrel (of wine)
Animal
Should be permitted

steps.confusionAlert: בְּרֵירָה is not about which partner is the 'real' owner. It asks whether dividing the item later lets us say each portion belonged to that partner from the moment יום טוב began.

phrases.english: What does Rav hold?
If he holds there is retroactive designation
even the animal should be permitted!
And if he holds there is no retroactive designation
even the barrel should also be forbidden!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי קָסָבַר רַב? אִי קָא סָבַר יֵשׁ בְּרֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the internal consistency of רב's ruling stated in Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that the barrel is permitted but the animal is forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two-sided dilemma: each possible position on בְּרֵירָה leads to the same ruling for both items, so a split ruling seems impossible.

steps.title: רב holds there is retroactive designation, but an animal is different
steps.stepSummary: רב holds יש ברירה. The animal is still forbidden because its parts feed each other, which mixes the two shares together again.
steps.simpleTranslation: Actually, he holds there is retroactive designation. But an animal is different, because the limits 'nurse' from each other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב. He holds יש ברירה, which is why the barrel is permitted, and it gives a special reason why the animal is still forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Wine in a barrel sits still, so once it is divided, each share is cleanly one partner's. A living animal is one body: every part draws nourishment from every other part until slaughter. Each partner's meat therefore contains something from the other's share, which is bound by the other person's limits, so the limits get mixed again.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually / really (introduces the true explanation)
It is different
They nurse / draw nourishment
שבת/יום טוב walking limits (here, the limits attached to each share)
From each other

phrases.english: Actually, he holds there is retroactive designation
but an animal is different
since the limits draw nourishment from each other.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְעוֹלָם קָסָבַר יֵשׁ בְּרֵירָה, וְשַׁנְיָא בְּהֵמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the dilemma in Step 11 by choosing one side, יש ברירה, and explaining the animal as an exception.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Picks one side of the dilemma and identifies a factual difference between the cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The barrel and the animal must follow the same בְּרֵירָה rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: בְּרֵירָה does apply to both, but in a living animal the shares mix again through shared nourishment, so the animal stays limited.

steps.title: רב כהנא and רב אסי object, and רב is silent
steps.stepSummary: If the shares in the animal really mix, that should also cause a מוקצה problem. Since no one worried about מוקצה, why worry about תחומין? רב gives no answer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב כהנא and רב אסי said to רב: About the prohibition of מוקצה they were not concerned, yet about the prohibition of תחומין they were concerned?! רב was silent.
steps.whatsHappening: Two students challenge רב's 'nursing' explanation from Step 12. רב does not respond.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If each partner's meat really contains part of the other partner's share, he ends up with meat he never had in mind for himself. That should make it מוקצה, yet the ruling allows the animal to be eaten. It is inconsistent to take the mixing seriously for תחומין but ignore it for מוקצה. רב's silence signals that the explanation is weakened.

keyTerms.meaning: Something set aside from use on שבת/יום טוב because it was not intended for use
They were concerned
He was silent

steps.confusionAlert: רב's silence is not a sign of agreement. In the גמרא, a silent response to a challenge usually means the challenge had no ready answer.

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרִי לֵיהּ רַב כָּהֲנָא וְרַב אַסִּי לְרַב:
phrases.english: Rav Kahana and Rav Asi said to Rav:
about the prohibition of muktze they were not concerned
yet about the prohibition of limits they were concerned?!
Rav was silent.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְאִיסּוּר מוּקְצֶה לֹא חָשְׁשׁוּ, לְאִיסּוּר תְּחוּמִין חָשְׁשׁוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer given in Step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that the animal's shares mix because its parts nourish each other
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Consistency: if the mixing were real, it would create a מוקצה problem as well, but no one is concerned about מוקצה here.
steps.whyThisMatters: Because רב's distinction goes unanswered, the גמרא moves on to ask what the final ruling is.

steps.title: What is the final ruling?
steps.stepSummary: Since רב's position was left unanswered, the גמרא asks what the conclusion is.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was concluded about it?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא asks for the bottom line on בְּרֵירָה and prepares to quote two אמוראים in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's middle position is now shaky, so the גמרא looks for the accepted view on whether בְּרֵירָה applies here at all.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the conclusion about it?

phrases.english: What was concluded about it?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי הָוֵי עֲלַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows רב's silence by asking for the final ruling.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether בְּרֵירָה applies to items bought in partnership, such as the barrel and the animal

steps.title: רבי הושעיא says there is retroactive designation, רבי יוחנן says there is not
steps.stepSummary: רבי הושעיא holds יש ברירה, so both items are permitted. רבי יוחנן holds אין ברירה, so both items are limited.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי הושעיא said: there is retroactive designation. And רבי יוחנן said: there is no retroactive designation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with two opposing views. Neither one draws רב's line between the barrel and the animal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to רבי הושעיא, each partner may carry his share of both the barrel and the animal according to his own limits. According to רבי יוחנן, both shares of both items are restricted to the area both partners may reach.

keyTerms.meaning: אמורא who holds יש ברירה in this first version (reversed in Step 19)
אמורא who holds אין ברירה in this first version (reversed in Step 19)

steps.whatToRemember: As first reported: רבי הושעיא holds יש ברירה (barrel and animal both permitted), and רבי יוחנן holds אין ברירה (both limited). Neither one supports רב's split ruling. This attribution is not final: step 19 reverses it (אפוך).

phrases.english: Rabbi Hoshaya said: There is retroactive designation.
And Rabbi Yochanan said: There is no retroactive designation.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי הוֹשַׁעְיָא אָמַר: יֵשׁ בְּרֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: This is a dispute: רבי הושעיא holds יש ברירה and רבי יוחנן holds אין ברירה.

steps.title: Challenge to רבי הושעיא from the משנה of the corpse in a house
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions whether רבי הושעיא really holds יש ברירה. It quotes a משנה about a corpse in a house with many doorways, where a person's later intention protects the other doorways.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does רבי הושעיא really hold there is retroactive designation? But we learned in a משנה: If a corpse is in a house that has many doorways, all of them are impure. If one of them was opened, that one is impure and all the rest are pure. If he intended to take the corpse out through one of them, or through a window that is four by four טפחים, this saves all the doorways.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a challenge to רבי הושעיא by quoting the source text it will use. Here it only quotes the משנה. The actual argument from it comes in Steps 17-18.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה teaches that טומאה spreads to every doorway the corpse might leave through. Once one exit is chosen, by actually opening it or just by deciding on it, the other doorways are pure. The גמרא will next examine how this choice works and what it implies for רבי הושעיא's view on בְּרֵירָה.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn in a משנה? (introduces a source used as a challenge)
The corpse
Doorways / entrances
He intended / planned in his mind
Four by four טפחים, the minimum size of a window that counts as an exit
It saves (protects from טומאה)

steps.confusionAlert: The doorways are not impure because the corpse touched them. They are impure because the corpse may later be carried out through them, so the טומאה is considered to spread toward every possible exit.

phrases.english: And does Rabbi Hoshaya hold there is retroactive designation?
But didn't we learn in a Mishnah:
A corpse in a house
and it has many entrances
all of them are impure.
If one of them was opened
it is impure, and all the others are pure.
If he intended to take it out through one of them

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ בַּחַלּוֹן שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ אַרְבָּעָה עַל אַרְבָּעָה
phrases.english: or through a window that is four by four handbreadths
it saves all the entrances.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְסָבַר רַבִּי הוֹשַׁעְיָא יֵשׁ בְּרֵירָה? וְהָתְנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רבי הושעיא's position stated in Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי הושעיא's view that יש ברירה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup stage: the גמרא quotes a משנה about choosing an exit for a corpse. Its argument about how a later choice works, and what that means for רבי הושעיא, follows in Steps 17-18.
steps.raayaSupportSource: משנה (אהלות) about a corpse in a house with many doorways

steps.title: The משנה continues: when must the person decide on the doorway?
steps.stepSummary: The quoted משנה ends with a dispute. בית שמאי say the decision about which doorway to use must be made before the person dies. בית הלל say it works even if made after death.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say: This only works if he decided before the person died. בית הלל say: It works even if he decided after the person died.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is still quoting the משנה it began quoting in the last step. It is setting up the real challenge, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the משנה taught that deciding which doorway the body will leave through keeps the other doorways pure. Now we learn that בית הלל allow this decision even after death, when the טומאה is already spreading. That makes us ask: does a late decision work backward in time, or only from then on?

keyTerms.meaning: The school of שמאי
The school of הלל
He thought or intended (decided in his mind)
The dead person (the corpse)

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say:
And this is only when he intended it (chose that doorway)
phrases.notes: He decided which doorway the body would be taken out through.

phrases.english: before the person died.
And Beit Hillel say:
Even after the person died.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: וְהוּא שֶׁחִשֵּׁב עָלָיו עַד שֶׁלֹּא יָמוּת הַמֵּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quotation of the משנה begun in Step 16 as the source for the challenge against רבי הושעיא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית הלל: a decision about the doorway made even after death still protects the other doorways.

steps.title: Rabbi Hoshaya says the decision works only from now on, not backward
steps.stepSummary: רבי הושעיא explains בית הלל: the later decision purifies the other doorways only from that moment forward. The גמרא infers that it does not work retroactively, so רבי הושעיא seems to hold אין ברירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was said about this משנה: רבי הושעיא said: It purifies the doorways from now on. From now on, yes. Backward in time, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings רבי הושעיא's explanation of the משנה and draws a sharp inference from his words. This is the punch of the challenge that began in Step 16.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי הושעיא held יש ברירה, the later choice would reveal that this doorway was the chosen one from the moment of death, so the other doorways would never have become טמא. He says it works only from now on, which means a later decision does not clarify the past. That is אין ברירה, the opposite of what Step 15 said he holds.

keyTerms.meaning: And it was stated about it (an אמורא's comment on a source)
Doorways or entrances
From here on (going forward only)
Retroactively, backward in time

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two directions. 'From now on' means the past is NOT clarified, and that is אין ברירה. יש ברירה would make the choice count backward in time.

phrases.english: And it was stated about it (this mishnah):
Rabbi Hoshaya said:
It serves to make the doorways pure
from now on.
From now on, yes,
phrases.notes: Here the גמרא is drawing an inference from רבי הושעיא's wording.

phrases.english: backward in time, no.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִתְּמַר עֲלַהּ, אָמַר רַבִּי הוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses רבי הושעיא's comment on the משנה quoted in Steps 16-17 to complete the challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 15's claim that רבי הושעיא holds יש ברירה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי הושעיא limits the later decision to 'from now on', which denies any backward clarification. That is אין ברירה, which contradicts Step 15.

steps.title: Reverse the opinions: רבי הושעיא holds no retroactive choice
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers by switching the two opinions. רבי הושעיא holds אין ברירה, and רבי יוחנן holds יש ברירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Reverse it: רבי הושעיא says there is no ברירה, and רבי יוחנן says there is ברירה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the contradiction by flipping who holds which view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 15 had רבי הושעיא as יש ברירה and רבי יוחנן as אין ברירה. Since the doorway case proves רבי הושעיא is אין ברירה, the גמרא swaps the names. Now רבי יוחנן becomes the one who holds יש ברירה.

keyTerms.meaning: Reverse it (switch the opinions)
Retroactive clarification: a later choice reveals what was designated from the start
Retroactive clarification works
Retroactive clarification does not work

steps.whyThisMatters: The reversal means the whole earlier conclusion about who permits and who limits now flips too, so the גמרא must check whether רבי יוחנן can really hold יש ברירה.

phrases.english: Reverse it:
Rabbi Hoshaya said: There is no retroactive clarification,
and Rabbi Yochanan said: There is retroactive clarification.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵפוֹךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of Steps 16-18 by reversing the attributions given in Step 15.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי הושעיא holds יש ברירה and רבי יוחנן holds אין ברירה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי הושעיא holds אין ברירה and רבי יוחנן holds יש ברירה.

steps.title: Does רבי יוחנן really hold retroactive choice? The brothers who divided
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the reversal. רבי יוחנן ruled that brothers who divide an inheritance are like buyers and must return the land to each other at יובל. That suggests he holds אין ברירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And does רבי יוחנן really hold ברירה? But רב אסי said in the name of רבי יוחנן: Brothers who divided an inheritance are buyers, and they return the land to each other at יובל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the new version from the last step by quoting another ruling of רבי יוחנן that seems to show he holds אין ברירה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי יוחנן held יש ברירה, the division would reveal that each brother's share was his directly from the father, so nothing would need to be returned. He instead calls them buyers, as if each brother bought his share from the others. Bought land goes back at יובל, so this ruling fits אין ברירה, not יש ברירה.

keyTerms.meaning: Does he really hold this? (opening of a challenge)
Brothers who divided (an inheritance)
Buyers or purchasers
The Jubilee year, when bought land returns to its original owner

phrases.aramaic: וּמִי אִית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בְּרֵירָה?
phrases.english: And does Rabbi Yochanan really hold retroactive clarification?

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַב אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן:
phrases.english: But didn't Rav Asi say in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
Brothers who divided (their inheritance)
are considered buyers,
phrases.notes: Each brother is treated as if he bought his share from the others.

phrases.english: and they return the land to each other in the Jubilee year.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אִית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בְּרֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reversal in Step 19 by citing a contradictory ruling of רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: Step 19's claim that רבי יוחנן holds יש ברירה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Calling the brothers buyers who return land at יובל means the division does not reveal that each share was inherited directly. That is אין ברירה, which contradicts Step 19.

steps.title: Maybe רבי יוחנן rejects ברירה only for Torah laws
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that רבי יוחנן says אין ברירה only for דאורייתא matters, like the inheritance and יובל case. For דרבנן matters he does accept ברירה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say: when does רבי יוחנן not hold of ברירה? Only in Torah laws. But in rabbinic laws, he does hold of it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a possible answer to the last challenge. It splits רבי יוחנן's view into two areas: Torah laws and rabbinic laws.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The inheritance case is about land returning at יובל, which is a Torah law. So רבי יוחנן's אין ברירה there does not have to apply to rabbinic matters. If he holds יש ברירה in rabbinic matters, the switch made in step 19 can still stand.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say. This introduces a suggested answer, often one that will be challenged.
Retroactive clarification: a later choice or event shows what was in effect all along.
A law from the Torah itself.
A law made by the Rabbis.

steps.confusionAlert: The phrase וכי תימא does not mean the גמרא has accepted this answer. It is only proposing it, and the very next line questions it.

phrases.english: And if you will say: when does he not hold
Rabbi Yochanan of retroactive clarification? In Torah laws,
phrases.notes: Like the inheritance and יובל case from step 20.

phrases.english: but in rabbinic laws, he does hold of it

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא: כִּי לֵית לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בְּרֵירָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 20 by limiting רבי יוחנן's אין ברירה to Torah laws.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the domain: Torah law versus rabbinic law.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן's inheritance ruling shows he rejects ברירה everywhere.
steps.terutzMaskana: He rejects ברירה only in דאורייתא matters and accepts it in דרבנן matters.

steps.title: Does רבי יוחנן really accept ברירה in rabbinic laws?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the split from step 21 and begins to bring a ברייתא taught by איו.
steps.simpleTranslation: But does he really hold of ברירה in rabbinic laws? Didn't איו teach otherwise?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the suggestion that רבי יוחנן accepts ברירה in rabbinic matters. It is setting up a quote from איו's ברייתא, which comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words והתני signal that a source is coming to argue against the suggestion. The source will be about עירוב תחומין, which is a rabbinic law, so it tests the split directly.

keyTerms.meaning: Does he really hold that? This is a doubting question.
But didn't he teach? This introduces a ברייתא used to challenge.
A Sage who taught ברייתות.

phrases.english: But in rabbinic laws, does he hold of it?
But didn't Ayo teach:

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבִדְרַבָּנַן מִי אִית לֵיהּ? וְהָתָנֵי אַיּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer from step 21.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יוחנן holds יש ברירה in דרבנן matters.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא about עירוב, which is rabbinic, seems to reject ברירה. This is about to be tied to רבי יוחנן.

steps.title: רבי יהודה allows a condition on where the חכם comes, but not on choosing between two חכמים
steps.stepSummary: In איו's ברייתא, רבי יהודה says a person cannot make one condition covering two opposite options at once. He may set two עירובין depending on where the חכם comes from. But if two חכמים come, one to each side, he may not choose later between them.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: A person cannot make a condition about two things at once. Rather: if the חכם comes to the east, his עירוב is in the east. If he comes to the west, his עירוב is in the west. But if one comes here and one comes there, it does not work.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the text of איו's ברייתא, the source behind the challenge. רבי יהודה allows one kind of double עירוב and forbids another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case, the person's own later choice plays no role: the next amud explains that it works because the חכם had already arrived when שבת began, so the fact was settled from the start. In the second case, the person wants to decide on שבת which חכם to go to, and that later choice would decide which עירוב worked from the start. That is ברירה, and רבי יהודה rejects it even though עירוב is only rabbinic.

keyTerms.meaning: Makes a condition.
Two things at once, meaning one condition covering two opposite options.
Here, an עירוב תחומין: food placed to set one's שבת 'home base' and extend walking distance. It is a rabbinic law.
Here and there, meaning two חכמים coming to two different places.

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה does not reject every double condition. He allows the case of one חכם whose direction is unknown. He forbids only the case where the person's own later choice between two חכמים would decide which עירוב works.
steps.whyThisMatters: עירוב is a rabbinic law, so a ruling against ברירה here challenges the idea that רבי יוחנן accepts ברירה in rabbinic matters. The link to רבי יוחנן comes on the next amud.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אָדָם מַתְנֶה עַל שְׁנֵי דְּבָרִים כְּאֶחָד,
phrases.english: A person may not make a condition on two things at once,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא: אִם בָּא חָכָם לַמִּזְרָח — עֵירוּבוֹ לַמִּזְרָח,
phrases.english: rather: if the Sage comes to the east, his eiruv is in the east,
if to the west, his eiruv is in the west,
but if one comes here and one comes there, it does not work.
phrases.notes: Here the person would choose on שבת between two חכמים. That is ברירה.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אֵין אָדָם מַתְנֶה עַל שְׁנֵי דְּבָרִים כְּאֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the content of the ברייתא introduced by והתני איו in step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: a double עירוב works when it depends on where one חכם comes from. It does not work when the person chooses later between two חכמים, because that would require ברירה, even in a rabbinic law.
